Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. Pathum Nissanka and Nishan Madushka are the openers for the Lankans. Hasan Mahmud has got the first new ball in his hand. Madushka to face. Here we go!

Welcome back. Time for the run chase. Sri Lanka have been asked to chase more or less the same score which they had set in the first ODI. For a major part of that run chase, Bangladesh looked largely untroubled and their collapse can only be put down to lack of application. The hosts will believe that they have got better batters than their opposition and will aim to seal the series tonight itself. If any, the ball swung a lot in the first few overs on Wednesday. If Bangladesh can use that to their advantage and take 2-3 quick wickets, the Lankans could be in a spot of self check.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, as we head into the second innings, Sri Lanka will fancy their chances of chasing this target. The pitch looks good for batting, and they will hope that it plays the same. However, Bangladesh do have a handy pace trio and some clever spinners, and if they strike early and apply pressure in the middle overs, this match can swing either way. Stay tuned for the gripping chase!

The credit for Bangladesh’s late stumble goes squarely to the Sri Lankan bowling unit, which was clinical and relentless. Asitha Fernando was exceptional with the new ball and at the death, claiming 4 wickets. Wanindu Hasaranga, the crafty leggie, once again spun his web and took 3 wickets, and broke crucial partnerships in the middle and end overs. Theekshana and Wellalage kept things tight, even without wickets, allowing others to attack. Overall, it was a well-rounded bowling display, where each bowler played his part and didn’t allow Bangladesh to run away with the game. Also, a special mention to the fielding of the players of Sri Lanka, who were exceptional in the field, from doing run-outs to taking some good catches and saving runs, all in all, they gave their best there.

Tawhid Hridoy stepped up under pressure and stitched another valuable stand with Emon before the latter fell to Hasaranga. Hridoy showed patience, anchoring the middle overs and slowly building up his innings before reaching a gritty half-century. But with heat and humidity wearing down the batters, Jaker Ali cramped up in the middle of his innings, and got out in the process. Despite late fireworks from Tanzim Hasan Sakib, the tail collapsed quickly. Bangladesh lost their last five wickets for just 44 runs, wasting the platform they had built in the first 20 overs.

Their innings started with early nerves as Tanzid Hasan, their standout performer from the first match, departed cheaply. But the pair of Parvez Hossain Emon and Najmul Hossain Shanto steadied the ship with a steady half-century partnership. Emon looked fluent and fearless, reaching his maiden ODI fifty. Shanto too looked composed before falling to skipper Asalanka at the wrong time. Mehidy Hasan Miraz’ poor form continued with the bat, falling for a single-digit score again, which pushed the pressure back on the middle order.

Bangladesh once again have found themselves repeating a familiar pattern, from a promising start to followed by a middle-order wobble and ending with a score that’s respectable but possibly below par. Opting to bat first, they showed intent early on but couldn’t convert their solid platform into something more substantial. After getting to 110/2 around the 20-over mark, with both batters set, they looked set to push well beyond 275 easily. However, Sri Lanka’s bowlers, particularly their spinners and death-over specialists, pulled things back sharply. Bangladesh have been bowled out for 248 in 45.5 overs, a total that feels competitive but not commanding, especially how the pitch has played, where the batters were playing shots through the line.

OUT! LBW! Excellent review by Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have left 25 balls unused. A touch short in length, outside off, Mustafizur Rahman stays back in his crease to defend but misses. The ball lands and spins back in, catching him on the pads. Hasaranga appeals and extends the same, but the umpire is as still as stone. The keeper, Kusal Mendis, is confident along with his bowler and skipper Charith Asalanka signals for the review. Nothing on UltraEdge when ball goes past the bat, while Ball Tracking shows it to be hitting the top of middle and leg sticks. The decision has to be overturned and the 30-run stand has been broken. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Well, the pitch might be more or less similar to the one featured in the first ODI, but definitely, the playing conditions are not the same. In the first match, Bangladesh got one of the two new balls to move around a lot till the 20th over at least, but there has barely been any movement here with either of the balls. Here and there, there was a one-odd case of the ball swinging but not much of concern to the batters. Additionally, spin has not yet had an effect. The wicket which fell was more due to lack of perfect execution by the batter. In short, this pitch does look like a terrific one to bat upon and the visitors will have to target somewhere in the region of 300 to be safe. Parvez Hossain Emon has got a start now and should be aiming for a three-digit score. It will be a challenge for the Lankans if the balls don't do much. The shot is already through before the ball could come and all the batter manages is a thick outside edge behind. The keeper, Kusal Mendis, dives in front to pouch that catch and Sri Lanka have their first wicket. PITCH REPORT - Russell Arnold is doing the pitch report. Arnold observes that during the first ODI, the pace got quicker and had more bounce in the evening, during the second innings. That practically means that batting in the second innings is a lot easier. Believes that the pitch is more or less similar to the one used in the first ODI and once again, spin will play a pivotal role. Reckons that the team batting first needs to score around 270-280 to win.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, wanted to bat first as well. Agrees that the pitch looks a good one to bat upon. On the top order's failure in the previous game, Asalanka says that there was a chat with the players, but at the same time, there is massive trust on the batters. Informs that the team has made two tactical changes, with Dunith Wellalage and Dushmantha Chameera coming in for Milan Rathnayake and Eshan Malinga.

The skipper of Bangladesh, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, says that they’ll bat first, backing the surface, which looks good and quite similar to the one used in the last match. He admits the previous result was an upset, but the team had honest conversations about bouncing back stronger. Mentions that they’ve come in well-prepared, as they know the conditions well. States that they had a couple of days for training coming up in this clash. Informs that the side has made two changes, where Shamim comes in place of Litton and Hasan comes in for Taskin, who is rested to manage his workload.

Talking about the weather, it was in talk during the first ODI, with as many as three players suffering from cramps. Tanvir Islam was struggling post his 4th over itself while Mustafizur Rahman literally did not complete his full quota of overs, and just walked out of the field due to cramps. From the Lankan camp, Wanindu Hasaranga was struggling as well. So we hope that the weather is a bit kinder to the players today. For now, it is bright, sunny and hot again.

Conditions in Colombo remain gloomy, and there are considerable chances of rain, but in patches for the full day. But fans will hope that the rain stays away, and they can get a full game. The pitch is expected to aid spin once again, but let’s see how it pans out with this weather. Stay tuned for the toss and more updates!

For Bangladesh, this match is all about handling pressure and executing better in key phases. Tanzid Hasan looked solid at the top, and Jaker Ali also fought hard down the order, but their middle-order collapse was alarming. They'll need a more measured approach against spin and better support for their bowlers. Former skipper Shanto has been dropped from the T20I squad, so he will come out to prove a point here. Also, they will play this match without their coach, Phil Simmons, who is unavailable due to personal reasons. With Taskin and Tanzim in form, Bangladesh certainly have the firepower to hit back, but it’ll require collective discipline.

Sri Lanka will be buzzing with confidence. Asalanka continues to lead by example, and their spinners, Hasaranga and Kamindu, have proven to be the real match-winners on a dry, gripping surface. After missing out on playing in the Champions Trophy earlier this year, this team is looking fierce as they want to prove their supremacy in the ODI format, as they have been a formidable side in the last two decades. Their batting depth and spin-heavy attack are perfectly suited to the Premadasa conditions. If they stay composed and start well again, Sri Lanka could easily close out the series here itself.

In the first ODI, Sri Lanka recovered from a shaky start after losing three wickets inside the Powerplay. Charith Asalanka anchored the innings beautifully, stitching vital partnerships with Kusal Mendis and Janith Liyanage. For Bangladesh, Taskin Ahmed and Tanzim Hasan Sakib were the pick of the bowlers. Chasing 245, Bangladesh were in control at 100 for 1 before Wanindu Hasaranga’s magical spell turned the tide. He took 4 wickets for just 10 runs in under eight overs, while Kamindu Mendis chipped in with a game-changing 3/19. The visitors collapsed dramatically from a position of strength, losing nine wickets for just 67 runs and ending at 167 all out.

Hello and welcome to the second ODI between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo. After a dominant win in the first game, the hosts have taken a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. Led by Charith Asalanka, Sri Lanka will now be eyeing a series win. On the flip side, it’s a must-win situation for Mehidy Hasan Miraz and his men. They had their moments in the opener but couldn’t capitalize, and now find themselves under pressure.

Sri Lanka are firmly in control as they head into the second ODI, riding high after a commanding 77-run win in Colombo. Captain Charith Asalanka starred with a composed century, while their spin twins Wanindu Hasaranga and Kamindu Mendis, alongside Maheesh Theekshana, dominated as the ball spun in the closing stages. Bangladesh, on the other hand, were left stunned after collapsing from a promising start losing seven wickets for just five runs - a collapse that highlighted their inconsistency and outdated middle-order. Sri Lanka will look to maintain their momentum with a balanced attack under home conditions. Pathum Nissanka who was the start in the Tests missed out in the first game and will want to make up while Kusal Mendis has been in good form but needs a big score. Bangladesh, embarking on a rebuilding journey without veterans like Mushfiqur and Mahmudullah, will turn to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, their new ODI captain, to instil belief. Their batting will hinge on the form of youngsters like Najmul Hossain Shanto, Tanzid Hasan, and Jaker Ali, all bursting with potential and the latter two showed that in the last game with fine knocks. Mehidy himself and Taskin Ahmed, fresh from a four-wicket haul, will lead the charge with the ball, but they will also need the experience of Mustafizur Rahman. The Tigers know they must find composure in key moments if they’re to force a series decider Expect Sri Lanka to continue using spin-friendly conditions to their advantage, while Bangladesh search for some middle-order stability and early breakthroughs. The series is young, the energy fresh and with pride and momentum on the line, this second ODI should be fiercely contested.
